An Ancient Greek mixing-bowl or cauldron, without handles or feet.

examples: That's Koops, from Petalburg. He's got confidence issues... He's a...cringer, y'know?

senses: Compromising material, blackmail material, (real or fabricated) evidence that a person does not want revealed, dirt.
ety: Borrowed from Russian компрома́т (kompromát), short for компромети́рующий материа́л (komprometírujuščij materiál, “compromising material”). Soviet security service slang from the Stalin era.
examples: Many observers have commented that, with so many Russian newspapers and TV channels now controlled by oligarchs or powerful organisations, kompromat is now a regular feature in the supposedly independent press.

senses: Meeting lexicographical standards or requirements; worthy of being included in a dictionary.
Dangling; tending to dangle.
Resembling or characteristic of a biscuit.
examples: Mouthfilling and creamy-smooth, it is peachy and slightly spicy, with biscuity, toasty notes in a high-flavoured, moderately complex style, for drinking now or cellaring.

senses: A close female friend, family member, or comrade.
ety: From Middle English sustren, plural of suster influenced by Old Norse systirin, plural of systir; the Old English plurals (of sweostor) were ġesweostor, ġesweostra, and ġesweostru. Analysable as sister + -en (plural ending).
examples: Come out of the dark and come into the light, sistren.

senses: Based on five tones.
examples: The middle movement is completely pentatonic, giving it an unusual sound.

senses: Derived; derivative.
ety: From Latin dērīvātus. Equivalent to derive + -ate (adjective-forming suffix).

senses: A violent storm in the Caribbean.
A violent force.
ety: From Spanish bayamo, from Bayamo, the capital city of the Granma Province of Cuba.
examples: There was a bayamo upon the Sea.

senses: Creation of any myth.
ety: From mytho- + -poeia, dated 1846 CE, based on Ancient Greek μυθοποιία (muthopoiía, “myth-making”).

senses: A gauzeless pipe for smoking cannabis, more like a Vietnamese Duc Lau than a bong.
Items designed to be bought as gifts
examples: The sole witness was the president of the petitioner corporation, an "Importer and manufacturer of lamps, giftwares, and artwares."
We owned a company called Black Is More Than Beautiful, a giftware company. We produced calendars and gift cards and things like that.

senses: A member of the lumpenproletariat.
ety: Shortened from German Lumpenproletariat, from Lump (“a contemptible person”) + Proletariat.

senses: The skin or hide of a kid, i.e., a young goat.
The leather made from such skins.
The box tree, Buxus sempervirens.
The hard, close-grained wood of this tree, used in delicate woodwork and in making inlays.
ety: From box + wood; box from Latin buxus (“box-tree, object made of boxwood”), of uncertain origin; compare Ancient Greek πύξος (púxos).

senses: Of a muscle, having two heads or points of origin.
A traditional administrative subdivision in Eastern Europe.
ety: Borrowed from Russian во́лость (vólostʹ) and Ukrainian во́лость (vólostʹ), from Old East Slavic волость (volostĭ).
examples: In 1923 Soviet Ukraine’s 102 povity were replaced by 53 larger okruhy (sing. okruha), and its 1,989 volosti by 706 raions.

Any member of the Helicobacter bacteria.
Any of many flat biscuits, or cakes, made from oatmeal.
a Staffordshire oatcake
A sunny region or landscape.
examples: The sunlands of the West and the spicelands of the East, the smiling Arcadias and blissful Islands of the Blest—ha! ha!

Exposure of an opponent's secret wickedness, especially in the opponent's presence.
ety: Borrowed from Late Latin, from Ancient Greek κατηγορία (katēgoría, “public accusation”). Doublet of category.

Vallisneria spp. in freshwater environments.

The hazel tree.

examples: He was one of the best caulkers around.

senses: A specialist in marketing (promoting and selling products and services).
One who promotes and sells products or services; called a marketer in US English.
Someone who works in or supports a certain kind of system of selling and buying, for example free marketeer, black marketeer.
Synonym of qilin; typically used in Japanese contexts.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 麒(き)麟(りん) (kirin), from Middle Chinese. Doublet of qilin.

senses: Drinking utensils that lack a stem, such as beer mugs.
Tools and accessories used for preparing or serving alcoholic drinks.
examples: The speakeasy—a common feature of many Prohibition-era homes—was transformed into an open bar area with plenty of sturdy, party-ready Mexican recycled glass barware.

senses: A full-body costume of a cartoon character (typically a mascot of cartoonish proportions) originating in Japan.
A full-body cosplay of a human cartoon character with realistic proportions paired with an anime-style mask, originating in Japan; also (metonymic), the anime-style mask used in such a cosplay.
A themed onesie, typically in the style of a cartoon animal.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese 着ぐるみ (kigurumi), from 着 (ki, “clothes, outfit”) + 包み (kurumi, “bundle, parcel”) (referring to the fact that the costume completely encloses the wearer).

senses: A gradual healing after illness or injury.
The period of time spent healing.
ety: Borrowed from Middle French convalescence, from Late Latin convalēscentia (“regaining of health”), from Latin convalēscēn(t-)s, present participle of convalēscere (“to become strong or well”); see convalesce.

senses: A Japanese paper lantern.
A system that notifies workers of a quality or process problem, sometimes with a means to pause production until the problem is resolved.
A light used to indicate a problem in the andon manufacturing system.
ety: (manufacturing): Borrowed from Japanese アンドン (andon), a specialization of 行灯 (andon). Introduced by Toyota.
